title: CPTAC STAD Study
summary:
The CPTAC gastric cancer study is the most extensively measured cohort indexed here. Four of its seven layers - acetylome, glycoproteome, ubiquitylome and metabolome - exist in fewer than twenty NCI cohorts each, and the combination on a single set of 193 tumors exists nowhere else. Ubiquitylation data on 184 cases is particularly scarce: only five studies in the entire Proteomic Data Commons carry it.
It is also a clear illustration of why reuse measurement is hard. All of it is openly downloadable with no account, and yet a literature search for its accession finds almost nothing - because authors cite the marker paper, not the PDC study identifier. The absence of citation evidence here says more about how proteomics data are referenced than about whether anyone has used them.
one_liner: 193 gastric cancers measured seven ways - proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome, glycoproteome, ubiquitylome, metabolome and protein-protein interaction - the deepest single-cohort molecular characterization in the NCI portfolio, and openly downloadable.

useful_for.question: How do distinct post-translational modification layers diverge from each other and from transcript abundance on the same tumors?
useful_for.rationale: Phosphorylation, acetylation, glycosylation and ubiquitylation are measured on largely the same 184 to 193 tumors. Comparing regulation across four modification types on one cohort is an analysis this dataset uniquely enables; almost every other resource offers at most two.
useful_for.statistical_note: Each layer has its own missingness pattern from mass spectrometry. Do not impute across layers; restrict to features quantified in a pre-specified fraction of samples and report that threshold.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Does protein degradation signaling, read from the ubiquitylome, identify tumor subgroups invisible to transcriptomics?
useful_for.rationale: Ubiquitylome data on 184 cases is among the largest such datasets anywhere. Degradation is a major regulatory axis that expression data cannot see, and a cohort this size makes subgroup discovery feasible rather than anecdotal.
useful_for.statistical_note: Ubiquitylation site quantification is sparser than proteome quantification; expect to lose a substantial fraction of sites to the completeness filter.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: How does tumor metabolism, measured directly rather than inferred, relate to signaling state?
useful_for.rationale: Metabolomics on 187 cases is available alongside the phosphoproteome, so metabolic state can be related to signaling directly instead of being inferred from enzyme transcript levels - which is what most metabolic analyses in cancer actually do.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Can measured protein-protein interaction data improve network inference over correlation-based approaches?
useful_for.rationale: Interaction data on 153 cases is exceptionally rare in a tumor cohort, and provides a measured reference against which inferred co-expression networks can be scored.

limitations.statement: The PDC record carries no clinical annotation: no survival, no treatment, no stage and no demographics are exposed through the study metadata.
limitations.mitigation: Clinical data for CPTAC cohorts are distributed through the Genomic Data Commons and the CPTAC data portal rather than PDC. Retrieve them separately and join on the case identifier before attempting any clinical claim.

limitations.statement: Each analytical fraction is a separate PDC study with its own sample set, so the seven layers do not cover an identical group of tumors - case counts range from 153 to 193.
limitations.mitigation: Build the intersection explicitly and report it. A complete-case analysis across all seven layers will be substantially smaller than 193.

limitations.statement: Layers were acquired with different enrichment chemistries and instrument methods, so batch structure differs between them and does not cancel out on integration.
limitations.mitigation: Model layer-specific batch covariates; do not concatenate raw intensities.

access_steps.action: Browse the study in the PDC portal
access_steps.detail: No account is required. All seven fractions are openly downloadable.

access_steps.action: Pull the study manifest from the PDC GraphQL API
access_steps.detail: The API is public and needs no key, which makes this cohort unusually easy to script against.
access_steps.cli_snippet:
curl -s https://proteomic.datacommons.cancer.gov/graphql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ allPrograms { name projects { name studies { pdc_study_id study_name analytical_fraction experiment_type cases_count } } } }"}' \
  | python3 -m json.tool | grep -A4 'CPTAC STAD'

access_steps.action: Retrieve the matching clinical and genomic data from the GDC
access_steps.detail: This is the step people skip. Without it the proteomic layers have no clinical context at all.

open_questions: PDC study identifiers are almost never quoted in the literature, so the reuse figure on this page is close to uninformative. A manual review of gastric proteogenomics papers would give a better estimate than any citation-based method.
